translation:
  text: 'III.1. “Sir,” I said, “I will add another question.” “Speak,” he said. “I heard from certain
    teachers,” I said, “that there is no other repentance[a] except the one when we went down into the
    water and received forgiveness of our former sins.”


    III.2. He said to me, “You heard correctly; that is how it is. A person who has received forgiveness
    of sins ought no longer to sin, but to live in purity.”


    III.3. “But since you examine everything closely, I will explain this too, without giving an opening
    to those who are going to believe or have now believed in the Lord. For those who have now believed
    or are going to believe have no repentance of sins, but they have forgiveness of their former sins.”[b]


    III.4. “The Lord therefore established repentance for those called before these days. For the Lord
    knows hearts and foreknows everything. He knew human weakness and the devil’s many schemes, that the
    devil would harm God’s servants and act wickedly against them.”[c]


    III.5. “So the Lord, being abundantly merciful, took pity on his creation and established this repentance.
    Authority over this repentance was given to me.”


    III.6. “But I tell you: after that great and solemn calling, if someone is tempted by the devil and
    sins, they have one repentance. But if they repeatedly sin and repent, it does not benefit such a
    person; they will live with difficulty.”[d]


    III.7. I said to him, “I have been brought to life by hearing these things from you so precisely.
    For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I will be saved.” “You will be saved,” he said, “and
    so will everyone who does these things.”


    IV.1. I asked him again, “Sir, since you have been patient with me, explain this too.” “Speak,” he
    said. “Sir,” I said, “if a woman or a man falls asleep in death and the surviving partner marries,
    does the one who marries sin?”[e]


    IV.2. “They do not sin,” he said. “But if someone remains unmarried, they gain greater honor and great
    glory for themselves with the Lord. Yet if they marry, they do not sin.”[f]


    IV.3. “So keep purity and reverence, and you will live to God. Keep everything I tell you and am going
    to tell you, from now on, from the day you were entrusted to me, and I will dwell in your house.”


    IV.4. “There will be forgiveness for your former trespasses if you keep my commandments. There will
    also be forgiveness for everyone if they keep these commandments of mine and walk in this purity.”[g]'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:

    text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted

    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“No repentance of sins, but forgiveness” retains the working printed text without softening
      its difficult distinction. Vulgata, Hilgenfeld (1873), physical61 printed42, has the corresponding
      repentance-of-sins contrast. The older 1891 apparatus instead reports Athos “no great sin”; alternative:

      their former sins.” Lake (1907), Plate V, prints repentance-of-sins in its later Athos transcription,
      so the reports disagree. The Sinaiticus project XML’s corresponding repentance/sins words are wholly
      or partly restored in a damaged span filed within chapter30.3, not an intact independent vote. Palatina
      paraphrases the passage differently; it is not silently converted into identical Greek testimony.'

      wording and many neighboring letters are editorially supplied or uncertain. Chapter31.5 partly preserves
      the authority/repentance statement; it is not a fully intact second text of the whole sentence.

  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working edition omits a negation that Athos has before repent. Lake (1907), Plate V line50,
      prints “and does not repent.” Alternative warning: “But if they repeatedly sin and do not repent,
      it does not benefit such a person; they will live with difficulty.” The positive reading is retained
      provisionally: Vulgata, Hilgenfeld physical61 printed42, says repeated sinning and doing repentance;
      Palatina, Gebhardt/Harnack (1877), physical180 printed83, speaks of frequently doing repentance.
      Sinaiticus breaks off within the preceding say-word and cannot decide the negation. Hypo cheira
      is rendered repeatedly in this context; “at once” is another possible idiomatic sense. The one-repentance
      statement and difficult-life warning are both retained. The older apparatus also reports Athos a
      calling-of-spirit expansion, absent from Lake’s later transcription; that report remains unresolved
      rather than being added to the main text.'
  - marker: e
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: 'Falls asleep is the death metaphor; the surviving partner makes explicit the implied person
      who marries, not the deceased spouse. More literal: “If a woman or a man falls asleep, and one of
      them marries, does the one who marries sin?” Palatina, physical182 printed85, explicitly distinguishes
      one dying and the other marrying. The respectful Sir is a printed correction of Athos’s conjunction
      at the opening; alternative opening: “And since you have been patient with me, explain this too.”
      Hapax can more literally mean once/already in the patience clause.'
  - marker: f
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Remains unmarried expresses remaining by oneself in the widowed context. The passage twice says
      marrying is not sin while also describing greater honor for remaining unmarried. Both claims are
      retained; no rule about every other marriage situation is added. Purity and reverence in the next
      paragraph render hagneia and semnotēs; chastity and dignity are alternatives.
  - marker: g

    text: 'The promise retains the stated conditions: keeping these commandments and walking in this purity.
      The everyone clause does not erase those conditions. The draft preserves both historical sections
      within legacy reader31; III/IV paragraph labels expose the boundary without changing reader IDs
      or overwriting legacy reader32.'

translation:
  text: 'III.1. “Sir, I have another question,” I said. “Speak,” he told me. I said, “Some teachers told
    me there is no other repentance[a] except when we went down into the water and received forgiveness
    of our former sins.”


    III.2. He said, “You heard correctly. That is how it is. Someone who has received forgiveness of sins
    should no longer sin. They should live in purity.”


    III.3. “You examine everything closely, so I will explain this too. I am not giving an opening to
    people who will believe or have now believed in the Lord. People who have now believed or will believe
    have no repentance of sins. But they have forgiveness of their former sins.”[b]


    III.4. “The Lord established repentance for people called before these days. He knows hearts and foreknows
    everything. He knew human weakness and the devil’s many schemes. The devil would harm God’s servants
    and act wickedly against them.”[c]


    III.5. “The Lord is abundantly merciful. He took pity on his creation and established this repentance.
    I was given authority over this repentance.”


    III.6. “But I tell you this. After that great and solemn calling, someone may be tempted by the devil
    and sin. They have one repentance. But if they repeatedly sin and repent, it does not benefit them.
    They will live with difficulty.”[d]


    III.7. I said, “Hearing this so clearly from you has brought me to life. If I add no more to my sins,
    I know I will be saved.” He said, “You will be saved. So will everyone who does these things.”


    IV.1. I asked again, “Sir, you have been patient with me. Explain this too.” “Speak,” he said. I asked,
    “If a woman or man falls asleep in death and the surviving partner marries, does that person sin?”[e]


    IV.2. “They do not sin,” he said. “If someone stays unmarried, they gain greater honor and great glory
    with the Lord. But if they marry, they do not sin.”[f]


    IV.3. “Keep purity and reverence, and you will live to God. Keep everything I tell you and will tell
    you. Do this from now on, from the day you were entrusted to me. I will dwell in your house.”


    IV.4. “Your former trespasses will be forgiven if you keep my commandments. Everyone will be forgiven
    if they keep these commandments of mine and walk in this purity.”[g]'

base_translation:
  text: 'III.1. “Sir,” I said, “I will add another question.” “Speak,” he said. “I heard from certain
    teachers,” I said, “that there is no other repentance[a] except the one when we went down into the
    water and received forgiveness of our former sins.”


    III.2. He said to me, “You heard correctly; that is how it is. A person who has received forgiveness
    of sins ought no longer to sin, but to live in purity.”


    III.3. “But since you examine everything closely, I will explain this too, without giving an opening
    to those who are going to believe or have now believed in the Lord. For those who have now believed
    or are going to believe have no repentance of sins, but they have forgiveness of their former sins.”[b]


    III.4. “The Lord therefore established repentance for those called before these days. For the Lord
    knows hearts and foreknows everything. He knew human weakness and the devil’s many schemes, that the
    devil would harm God’s servants and act wickedly against them.”[c]


    III.5. “So the Lord, being abundantly merciful, took pity on his creation and established this repentance.
    Authority over this repentance was given to me.”


    III.6. “But I tell you: after that great and solemn calling, if someone is tempted by the devil and
    sins, they have one repentance. But if they repeatedly sin and repent, it does not benefit such a
    person; they will live with difficulty.”[d]


    III.7. I said to him, “I have been brought to life by hearing these things from you so precisely.
    For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I will be saved.” “You will be saved,” he said, “and
    so will everyone who does these things.”


    IV.1. I asked him again, “Sir, since you have been patient with me, explain this too.” “Speak,” he
    said. “Sir,” I said, “if a woman or a man falls asleep in death and the surviving partner marries,
    does the one who marries sin?”[e]


    IV.2. “They do not sin,” he said. “But if someone remains unmarried, they gain greater honor and great
    glory for themselves with the Lord. Yet if they marry, they do not sin.”[f]


    IV.3. “So keep purity and reverence, and you will live to God. Keep everything I tell you and am going
    to tell you, from now on, from the day you were entrusted to me, and I will dwell in your house.”


    IV.4. “There will be forgiveness for your former trespasses if you keep my commandments. There will
    also be forgiveness for everyone if they keep these commandments of mine and walk in this purity.”[g]'
